The series has unstable ranking (tau -0.068) and strong seasonality, so a more aggressive weighting like softmax_neg_error may exploit subtle differences.
Test a robust DBA combination to see if it outperforms the weighted softmax, given the unstable ranking and strong seasonal trend.
Test a robust trimmed‑mean that may reduce influence of the few very high‑error models, given the unstable ranking and strong seasonal trend.
Use a robust median combination over the full model pool to test a different aggregation type, given the unstable ranking and strong trend/seasonality.
use inverse_error weights on a stable, diverse subset
The series has unstable ranking and strong seasonality; a per‑horizon best‑model weighting could adapt to horizon‑specific strengths.
The ranking is unstable and the best models cluster into two groups; a simple mean over the stable subset pool4 may yield a robust combination.
The series has unstable ranking and strong seasonality; a per‑horizon top‑k mean may capture horizon‑specific strengths while remaining robust.
The series shows unstable ranking but strong seasonality; a robust weighted combo on a diverse subset may improve over trimmed mean.
The series has strong trend/seasonality but unstable ranking; a robust trimmed mean over a stable subset (pool4) may outperform the full‑pool trimmed mean by reducing variance from noisy models.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.8602. Series context: trend strength 0.9992 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.068); 4 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 1.435.
